title: Choose a target that cannot move

D0.outcome: Explains that an attack should aim at something that cannot step aside (a pinned piece, a fixed pawn).

D1.outcome: Finds the target in a given position (a fixed backward pawn, a pinned piece) and the squares to attack it from.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, chooses between harassing a movable piece with pawns (losing time) and fixing a target; recognises when a chase pays.

D3.outcome: Counts attackers against defenders on the fixed target and sees when a pawn break can free it.

misconceptions: Kicking a piece with a pawn always gains time.
sources: sources/sheets/edlasker_chess-strategy.md §4 K15, K16; §7 row K15; §8 item 8
conditions: The target really cannot evade, or the chase does not weaken the pawn skeleton or send pieces offside.
contrasts: The pawn kick lets the piece retreat to an equal square and leaves a backward pawn.
Chasing a piece to gain space or put it offside is accepted dynamic play, so 'never chase' is wrong.
A piece with no good squares anyway.
